title: Weeping Fig: Old Weeping Figs You Can Visit
meta_description: A weeping fig in Queensland grew wide enough to double as the town's milk depot and war memorial shelter. Three weeping figs mapped.
intro: The genuinely large, old weeping figs people go to see split into two very different stories. In Miriam Vale, Queensland, on the coast road to Agnes Water, one fig has grown to roughly 12 metres round and 35 metres across, doing duty since around the 1890s as the town's milk depot, its war memorial shelter and an impromptu vet's surgery, all under one crown. Brisbane's stands at the Alice Street gate of the City Botanic Gardens, about 155 years old, planted not long after the gardens themselves were founded, native ground for a species that grows wild across northern Australia and South and Southeast Asia. Lisbon's is the odd one out, five metres round in the Campo de Santana park, doing the same unlikely, enormous work eight thousand kilometres from where the species grows on its own. All three keep their leaves year-round and none has ever stopped spreading wider rather than taller, which is the whole trick of the tree.
